claims.statement: Management targets an R&D spend around 6% going forward.
claims.quote: I think the normal range which we have been operating in is around 5% to 6% of R&D spend. It gets lumpy at times, depending on certain programs where the R&D and API costs might get lumpy. But I think we will try and keep it more around that 6%.
claims.speaker: management

claims.statement: Management expects two respiratory products in the next 6 months to potentially be among the company's largest revenue products.
claims.quote: What I was trying to say is that it's quite likely that one, if not both, could be one of the largest products for the Company. That's what I was trying to say. So, if you take out Lenolidomide, right? And if you take the next top 2 or 3 products of the company that we sell, including Lanreotide, this is ballpark in that top 2 or top 3 product type of a profile for revenue.
claims.speaker: management
claims.target: top 2 or top 3 product type of a profile for revenue

claims.statement: Management expects full-year benefits from the cost reduction program to start kicking in next year.
claims.quote: Part of that program, some benefit may come towards the end of this year, but more full year benefits will start kicking in the next year.
claims.speaker: management

claims.statement: Management does not anticipate any material adjustments to the Rs. 275 crores exceptional item.
claims.quote: So, we don't anticipate any material adjustments to this amount.
claims.speaker: management

facts.statement: The company has been averaging a gross margin of about 65%, with a typical range of 60% to 65%.
facts.quote: No, see I think we have been averaging about 65% or so. So, range of about 60%-65%, depending on the mix, some quarters will have more acute.

facts.statement: R&D expenses include material costs, other costs, people costs, and litigation costs for products in the US and other countries.
facts.quote: So, all the three line items will have those sitting. So, if you see increase in those line items, that's also because of R&D. Not so much in people, because we have not really invested big time in people on the R&D side, but on material and other expenses increased, you can see it's on account of R&D. And R&D also has litigation costs that you do for the products in the US or any other country.

facts.statement: The Galvus capital commitment of 1,100 sits in the capital commitment in note 38 of the balance sheet.
facts.quote: That sits in the capital commitment in our balance sheet in note 38, that clarifies the amount that is sitting there for Galvus capital commitment that we have made.

facts.statement: Schedule M implementation raises quality standards for manufacturing, impacting smaller players while Cipla is already at or better than required standards.
facts.quote: It is more of an impact for smaller players who will need to ramp up to meet those quality standards. From CIPLA perspective, we do not have much or any impact because we are already at or better than the standards that are asked for.
